transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-08-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Torres (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Lena Park (HavenWorks Head of MLOps), Carlos Mendes (CTO), Priya Singh (Procurement)

Auto-summary (may be rough): HavenWorks wants to tack on EU and APAC capacity, push committed capacity up ~20%, and run an on-prem pilot for regulated PHI processing. Procurement asks for SOC2, KMS/HSM doc, and sample SLA amendment. SE to run quick synthetic to validate tail latency at 16k token lengths.

[00:00] Ava Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, we'll run through where you are on renewal and the expansion asks, and miguel will cover the tech plan.
[00:12] Lena Park: hi! lena here, i'll start — we are about to renew in october and wanted to lock in capacity plus add two regions, eu-west and apac-sin, and also discuss an on-prem pilot for our PHI-heavy flows.
[00:25] Carlos Mendes: yeah, timeline is tight because compliance calendar. procurement needs pricing and SOC2 evidence by mid-aug.
[00:32] Priya Singh: and we need a clear contract amendment for the committed uplift.
[00:37] Miguel Torres: ok got it. quick clarifying q — when you say on-prem pilot, are you thinking private control plane or full air-gapped?
[00:45] Lena Park: short term private control plane into our VPC, maybe on-prem later if pilot proves results. we need KMS integration — we use KeySafe HSM, so key wrapping and CMEK is essential.
[00:58] Miguel Torres: ok we support KMS via customer-managed keys, it's handled in the private deployment docs, though sometimes nuance on HSM providers needs handshake. i'll note KeySafe.
[01:08] Ava Chen: to set expectations on numbers, you're looking at about 20% uplift vs current baseline and two additional regions; that maps to a dedicated node count increase and a different SLA path. pricing table will show the reserved capacity commit.
[01:22] Carlos Mendes: can you remind us difference between hosted + dedicated + private — for latency / cost tradeoffs?
[01:30] Jordan Lee: yeah briefly — hosted is quickest to onboard but less isolation; dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput; private (VPC or on-prem) gives full control and KMS/HSM integration but has setup lead time and higher unit cost.
[01:45] Carlos Mendes: right, we care a lot about p95 tail latency for long-context prompts — the legal assistant has ~12-16k tokens sometimes.
[01:54] Miguel Torres: noted. our runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache but long context workloads need careful tuning; for 16k we recommend a mix of quantization and sharded KV handling to keep tails under 350-450ms in EU nodes, depends on model.
[02:10] Lena Park: hmm 350-450ms, is that realistic? their current self-hosted infra sometimes spikes.
[02:16] Miguel Torres: it's best-effort estimate; we'll run a 48hr synthetic against your typical prompt mix to calibrate.
[02:22] Priya Singh: procurement will also need a data residency clause for EU traffic — logs stay in region except audit exports, is that possible?
[02:30] Ava Chen: yes we can scope residency; for hosted we pin region; for private we can ensure logging to customer-managed S3 in eu-west. audit exports can be controlled via role-based access.
[02:40] Carlos Mendes: on the SOC2 front — do you have the latest report? our security requests the full attestation and a list of subservice orgs.
[02:49] Ava Chen: yes, we'll send the SOC2 report and the security pack after. note that the private deployment adds extra items but we can provide architecture diagrams and KMS integration notes.
[02:58] Lena Park: perfect. also curious about failover — if eu node has a capacity event do you failover to us-west or to a cheaper model? we need deterministic failover policies.
[03:10] Miguel Torres: you can set routing policies: prefer region, fallback to lower-cost model variant, or stall and queue. for regulated flows you likely want strict region-only failover to another EU availability zone. we can set that in the routing policy.
[03:22] Priya Singh: pricing question — is the reserve commit monthly or annual? we prefer annual for predictability but want to avoid overcommit.
[03:29] Ava Chen: we offer monthly and annual committed options; annual comes with discount tiers. given your upcoming ramp we can craft a step-up commit across quarters — e.g., 10% now, additional 10% after pilot validates.
[03:45] Carlos Mendes: that sounds reasonable, procurement will want examples of cost per token with and without quantization.
[03:51] Miguel Torres: we'll include quantization profiles and impact on quality + throughput in the worksheet. be aware heavy quantization influences hallucination risk — but usually fine for deterministic extraction tasks.
[04:05] [04:05] Speaker 1: (background) yeah...
[04:10] Lena Park: another technical ask — do you keep KV cache across restarts, or is it ephemeral? for us persistence reduces repeated compute.
[04:18] Miguel Torres: KV cache persisted in dedicated runtimes if enabled; in hosted ephemeral caches might expire. for private on-prem we can enable persisted cache backed by your storage. small caveat — persisted cache requires coordination for cache invalidation on model updates.
[04:36] Carlos Mendes: ok noted. could you run a test with our 3 sample prompts? we'll upload them to the benchmark sheet.
[04:44] Ava Chen: yes please share prompts; miguel will run them in synthetic.
[04:48] Priya Singh: legal also mentioned they need retention windows for logs. can you support 90/180/365 day retention?
[04:55] Jordan Lee: yes configurable retention is available; for private deployments retention can be fully controlled by you.
[05:02] Miguel Torres: i'll also note that for PHI workloads we recommend private VPC with CMEK and restricted audit logs.
[05:10] Lena Park: on the on-prem pilot — our infra can provision a bare-metal rack; we want Redwood runtime dockerized to ship. is that supported?
[05:19] Miguel Torres: we provide containerized bundles for private customers; there is an ops checklist — network, storage, GPUs, KMS endpoint. lead time usually 4-6 weeks for on-prem pilot hardware validation.
[05:33] Carlos Mendes: that's a bit long, can we expedite? our compliance window is aggressive.
[05:38] Ava Chen: we can prioritize staging resources if you're willing to sign a short pre-provision addendum; i'll put options in the pricing worksheet.
[05:47] Priya Singh: procurement needs to see SLA changes for committed capacity — p99 latency targets and credits.
[05:54] Jordan Lee: we'll include a sample SLA amendment with p95/p99 targets and credit formulas. note that heavier context lengths shift expected tail numbers.
[06:04] [06:04] Carlos Mendes: can you share a recent benchmark sheet? i want to see raw numbers for 8k and 16k tokens across EU nodes.
[06:12] Miguel Torres: yes i'll attach the last run, but it used a slightly different model; we'll run one with your prompts.
[06:18] Lena Park: one more blocker — network egress costs in apac were higher in past vendors. how are those handled?
[06:25] Ava Chen: egress is typically passed through; for Dedicated and Private we can negotiate egress allowances or you can route through your peering to reduce egress. we'll add guidance.
[06:36] Priya Singh: procurement Q — is there a minimum term for reserved nodes?
[06:40] Ava Chen: standard reserved commitments are 12 months, but we can do quarterly ramp plans under a flexible commit if you need.
[06:47] Carlos Mendes: ok, i think we have the high-level. can we outline the pilot acceptance criteria?
[06:52] Miguel Torres: sure, suggested acceptance criteria: 1) p95 latency under 400ms for common prompts, 2) no more than 2% error rate on deterministic extraction tasks, 3) successful KMS key-wrapping integration and audit log delivery to your S3.
[07:08] Lena Park: those look good. add a quality metric for hallucination/incorrect extractions being under 1%.
[07:15] Miguel Torres: added.
[07:18] Priya Singh: procurement also wants an attached data processing addendum and flow chart for PHI handling.
[07:24] Ava Chen: we'll include DPA and a PHI handling flow chart in the security pack.
[07:30] [07:30] Speaker 2: (murmur)
[07:36] Carlos Mendes: out of curiosity, did anyone try switching to the Redwood-optimized quantized models? we saw some quality differences in a previous vendor test.
[07:45] Miguel Torres: we maintain model profiles; quantized models have slight deltas but often negligible for extraction tasks. we'll include quality comparisons.
[07:55] Lena Park: ok great. timeline recap?
[07:58] Ava Chen: summary timeline: pricing worksheet and SOC2/security pack by 2027-08-09, Miguel runs 48h benchmark starting 2027-08-10 and shares results by 2027-08-12, pilot kickoff tentative 2027-08-18 pending procurement sign-off.
[08:14] Carlos Mendes: procurement will try to mirror that timeline.
[08:17] Priya Singh: i will aim to confirm internal approvals by 2027-08-11.
[08:21] Miguel Torres: quick note on technical: for the benchmark we'll need temporary API keys and an ephemeral staging VPC or a Redwood test cluster to run against; which do you prefer?
[08:31] Lena Park: staging in our VPC with a peered test cluster is preferable so metrics reflect real network. we'll provide connectivity details.
[08:39] Miguel Torres: perfect, i'll send a connectivity checklist post-call.
[08:44] Ava Chen: any pushback or open concerns?
[08:48] Carlos Mendes: just the usual: speed of on-prem deploy and procurement turnaround.
[08:52] Lena Park: and network egress clarity.
[08:55] Ava Chen: understood — we'll surface egress examples in the worksheet.
[09:00] Jordan Lee: i'll add a note about failover policies for region-bound flows.
[09:06] Priya Singh: thanks all.
[09:09] Ava Chen: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with docs and schedule.

Meeting close.

References & attachments mentioned:
- "Pricing worksheet (to be shared)"
- "SOC2 + Security pack (to be shared)"
- "Benchmark plan and sample prompts sheet"
- "Private deployment ops checklist"

Notes about transcript quality: intermittent speaker overlap, minor mis-transcriptions (e.g., KeySafe HSM spelled 'KeySafe' correctly but vendor references might be off), timestamps approximate.
